summary: Overall, the notebook is high quality: it runs end-to-end, is well organized, and uses standard best practices (reproducible split, preprocessing inside a single pipeline) that reduce the risk of data leakage. The most important finding is that while the model’s AUC is decent (~0.73), recall is low at the default 0.5 threshold—meaning it will miss many churners unless the threshold is adjusted, which she correctly identifies and discusses. The conclusions are consistent with the outputs and tie model drivers (contract type, complaints, late payments) back to the exploratory analysis in a business-relevant way. In the interview, verify she can explain how she chose/should choose a threshold given business costs, and how she would validate the model over time (e.g., temporal split) and handle class imbalance beyond reporting AUC.

The candidate also acknowledges class imbalance by reporting AUC (cell 8) and explicitly discusses threshold calibration given low recall (cell 10), and cleaning addresses stated data messiness (cell 3).

justifications.C3: Written claims match executed outputs: the conclusion cites AUC 0.729 (cell 10) which matches the produced AUC_TEST=0.729 (cell 8; also confirmed in metricas_reais). No other numeric claims contradict the executed metrics or outputs.
justifications.C4: Conclusions are evidence-backed and business-relevant: key drivers cited (monthly contracts, complaints, late payments) align with the largest-magnitude coefficients shown (cell 9) and the churn-rate EDA supports contract-type differences (cell 5). The recommendation is actionable and limitations are appropriately stated (low recall at 0.5 threshold; lack of temporal validation) in cell 10.
